transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Security), Samantha Park (CISO - CardioHealth), Raj Patel (Head of Platform), Lina Gomez (Legal Counsel)

Summary (auto): quick security review focused on data residency and region pinning; clarified cross-border processing concerns, sub-processor list, KMS/encryption model, and next steps to run a PoC in eu-west-1.

Transcript:
[00:00] Emily Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm emily from redwood, i own the account, and with me is marcus our solutions engineer and priya who focuses on security, i'll let them quick intro 
[00:12] Marcus Alvarez: hey all, marcus, infra and performance, i'll be the one doing the region-pinning PoC if we move forward, hi 
[00:18] Priya Singh: priya here, security engineer, i usually handle SOC 2 / iso questions and kms design stuff
[00:25] Samantha Park: thanks, i'm samantha, ciso at cardiohealth; we've got raj and lina on the call too, we're mainly here because we need clear answers on where data lives and how you prevent cross-border transfer 
[00:36] Raj Patel: yep, hi, quick context - our platform is in aws, primary in us-east-1, but we have eu customers and legal wants model inference and any persisted artifacts to stay in eu-west-1 for those accounts
[00:48] Lina Gomez: and from legal perspective we need sub-processor list and DPA language that covers data residency plus any transfers to third parties

[01:05] Emily Chen: totally, that's a common ask. at a high level, redwood supports region pinning — you can pin requests to a region for processing, and we offer dedicated private deployments for stricter requirements. for hosted customers we do provide region routing and data residency controls, there are a few nuances around logging and backups i'll cover with priya

[01:25] Marcus Alvarez: to add, our routing policy can be configured at the customer or route level: you can pin generation calls to eu-west-1, for embeddings we can pin too. latency varies slightly but it's predictable; i'll run a small benchmark as we discussed

[01:40] Samantha Park: when you say "pin" do you actually prevent any data from leaving the region? eg, any calls to third-party sub-processors or metrics pipelines?

[01:50] Priya Singh: good question. short answer: for hosted region pinning we keep model inference and kv/prefix caches in the region; persistent logs and metric exports are configurable — by default certain operational metrics aggregate to our control plane (us-east) for analytics, but we can enable local-only logs and restricted telemetry for customers requesting it. we also offer private deployments where the control plane can be customer-managed in a VPC so nothing leaves your network if that's required

[02:20] Raj Patel: okay, so the default control plane aggregates metrics back to us-east - is that considered "cross-border" under eu rules? we need to be careful about GDPR and onward transfer to subprocessors

[02:33] Priya Singh: yes, it can be. we document that in the DPA. for eu-resident data we can do two things: 1) enable eu-only telemetry and local log retention, 2) provide a private control plane option or dedicated deployment in eu region. both reduce (or eliminate) cross-border transfer. many customers who need strict residency pick the private or dedicated option

[02:55] Lina Gomez: what about subprocessors - who are they, and do they include cloud providers like aws and monitoring vendors?

[03:05] Emily Chen: our current sub-processor list includes cloud infra providers (AWS/GCP), telemetry vendors for optional analytics, and a small set of security tooling providers. i'll share the full list and the contract language. we maintain SOC 2 and ISO artifacts for the infra and redwood services

[03:20] Samantha Park: can you confirm SOC 2 scope specifically — does it include the control plane and dedicated infra? we need to map controls to our audit

[03:28] Priya Singh: yes, our SOC 2 covers the hosted control plane and our managed services; dedicated/reserved capacity is included when managed by redwood. private/on-prem deployments are different: the control plane responsibility shifts — we provide the artifacts and guidance but customer-run control planes may fall outside our SOC scope. i'll flag that in the docs

[03:50] Marcus Alvarez: on KMS, we support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. you can bring your own KMS in the eu region and we can configure the workforce to use it. for in-flight data, we use TLS with mutual auth for service-to-service communication. there are some implementation details with cache encryption and kv-store snapshots i can walk through

[04:12] Raj Patel: so if we bring our own KMS in eu-west-1, does any key material cross to us-east?

[04:18] Priya Singh: no, the intent is keys remain in the region. our service negotiates with regional KMS endpoints; if you're on hosted we may still have metadata in the control plane but the data blobs and key ops can be region-scoped. for highest assurance we recommend private deployment or a dedicated tenant in eu-region with CMK configured

[04:40] Samantha Park: what about audit logs — we need immutable audit trail for access and admin actions, ideally stored in our eu-s3 and accessible via our SIEM

[04:48] Priya Singh: we can stream audit logs to your customer-owned sinks in eu (s3, splunk, datadog) — we support signed delivery and can set retention. logs include request metadata, user id, api key usage, and admin actions. there is an option to redact model outputs from logs if that's required for PHI/PII concerns

[05:10] Marcus Alvarez: on performance tradeoffs — when you pin to eu-west-1 and use a CMK, you'll see minimal latency delta for inference; the bigger delta is if you require a private control plane or on-prem because that changes network hop patterns and our fallbacks. i'll quantify in the PoC

[05:28] Raj Patel: curious about cross-border subprocessors — you mentioned telemetry earlier. if we enable local logs, does redwood still call any external analytics endpoints in us?

[05:38] Priya Singh: not if we configure eu-only telemetry. default onboarding tends to enable aggregated telemetry to help with debugging, but it's opt-in/opt-out and we document the flow. we'll mark the telemetry option in the PoC config so you can see exactly what would flow where

[05:55] Lina Gomez: on contract side, we need DPA with explicit region commitments and sub-processor notification windows. also proof of SOC 2 and an incident response SLA

[06:05] Emily Chen: absolutely, we'll share our DPA template, SOC 2 report (redacted), and incident response SLAs. we'll also surface the subprocessors and how we handle notifications for changes

[06:18] Samantha Park: one more - if there's a model fallback (eg capacity constrained in eu) and requests get routed to us-east fallback, is there a way to prevent that or fail closed? not acceptable to have eu requests leave the region

[06:30] Marcus Alvarez: good callout. we have routing policies that allow you to set strict pinning (fail closed) or soft pinning (fallback allowed). by default we use soft pinning for availability, but we can enforce hard pinning for accounts that require it; availability SLA differs when fail-closed is used

[06:50] Raj Patel: SLA impact?

[06:53] Emily Chen: if you choose fail-closed, your availability SLA is tied to region capacity; we can offer dedicated/reserved capacity to back that SLA and provide an SLA addendum. we'll include options in pricing and the PoC spec

[07:08] Lina Gomez: please include sub-processor contract language that allows us to audit or request evidence within 30 days if needed

[07:15] Priya Singh: we have a standard clause, but we can propose a 30-day evidence window for enterprise customers — i'll add it to the submission

[07:25] Emily Chen: recap — we'll send: 1) SOC 2 & DPA plus sub-processor list, 2) KMS architecture and guidance for CMK in eu-west-1, 3) PoC run plan for region pinning (eu-west-1) and performance/cost sheet, 4) options for fail-closed vs soft pinning and SLA/price impacts. any additions?

[07:44] Samantha Park: sounds good. please make sure the PoC includes log streaming to our eu-s3 and that model outputs are redacted from logs by default

[07:52] Marcus Alvarez: noted, will include that in the test config.

[07:57] Emily Chen: ok next steps and timeline?

[08:00] Samantha Park: we'd like the docs by monday, and the PoC the following week if possible

[08:05] Emily Chen: we'll aim to send SOC2/DPA + sub-processor list by 2027-01-17, priya will send KMS diagram by 2027-01-20, marcus will begin PoC the week of 2027-01-18 and share results by 2027-01-22. we'll schedule follow-up with raj's infra team on 2027-01-29 (two weeks out).

[08:25] Lina Gomez: thanks everyone, that covers it from legal, we'll review DPA and revert

[08:30] Samantha Park: thanks, appreciate it.

[08:32] Emily Chen: thank you all, we'll follow up with the pack.

End of transcript.
